title: Organize Your Poms In Clo | Clo Feature Deep Dive
description:

markdown_content: # Organize Your POMs in CLO | Clo Feature Deep Dive This document provides a detailed explanation of the updated Points of Measure (POMs) management features in CLO, including folder organization, adding and editing POMs, grading visibility, 2D and 3D measurement comparisons, and saving/loading measurement data. --- ## POMs Folder Organization in CLO This section covers how to organize Points of Measure (POMs) in CLO using folders for better management and workflow efficiency. - CLO now supports folders within the POM tab, similar to the fabric folder structure. - To create a new folder for POMs, click the "Create New Folder" icon. - After naming the folder, you can add POMs directly inside it via the add button. - POMs can be moved between folders easily using drag-and-drop functionality. - Folder options include: - Minimizing/collapsing folders using the arrow icon. - Deleting folders with two choices upon deletion: - Move contained POMs to the first folder. - Delete all POMs inside the folder along with the folder itself. - This folder organization helps keep POMs structured and manageable, especially in complex projects. --- ## Adding and Editing POMs This section explains how to add new Points of Measure and customize their measurement types in CLO. - To add a POM, use the add button within a folder or the main POM panel. - Example: Adding an "Armhole" POM involves: 1. Creating the POM entry. 2. Selecting start and end points on the garment for measurement. 3. Pressing enter to confirm. - The "Edit Point of Measure" tool allows further customization: - Right-click on the measurement segment to "Show Length" for a numeric value. - Change the segment type to a curve instead of a straight line via the context menu. - This flexibility allows accurate and specific measurements to be taken on the garment model. --- ## Viewing and Comparing 2D and 3D Measurements This section focuses on toggling and comparing 2D pattern measurements versus 3D garment measurements within CLO. - CLO displays both 3D garment measurements and 2D pattern measurements for each POM. - The "3D Line" checkbox toggles the visibility of 3D measurements on the garment. - When unchecked, only 2D measurements are visible. - The property editor below shows detailed measurement values: - Total 3D length. - 2D length. - The difference between 3D and 2D measurements (e.g., 1.344 units difference). - This feature helps identify discrepancies between pattern dimensions and actual garment fit, useful for grading and fit adjustments. --- ## Grading Visibility and Management This section describes how grading data integrates with POMs and how to manage its visibility. - If grading is applied to the garment, CLO shows graded measurements at the top of the POM list. - Graded sizes can be hidden or shown using the eye icon. - Hiding graded sizes allows a cleaner view of base measurements for easier editing and comparison. - Grading visibility can be toggled on or off to suit user preferences during the measurement and adjustment process. --- ## Saving and Importing POM Data This section explains how to save and load POM data, including support for Excel and CSV formats. - POM data can be saved via the save button in the POM tab. - Users can choose to save 2D measurements, 3D measurements, or both simultaneously. - Saved files retain folder groupings and show measurements across grading sizes (e.g., Small to Extra Large). - CLO can import Excel or CSV files containing POM data. - Imported files automatically populate measurement names and values, which then can be connected to garment points. - This import/export feature streamlines data management and integration with external measurement sources. --- # Summary CLO's enhanced POM management introduces folder organization, flexible point addition and editing, clear 2D/3D measurement comparison, grading visibility controls, and robust save/load capabilities with Excel and CSV support. These updates improve workflow efficiency, accuracy, and data handling for garment measurement and fitting tasks.
